newsitem.title: RWANDA: Rwandan women allege massacre by Zaire soldiers.
newsitem.headline: Rwandan women allege massacre by Zaire soldiers.

text.p: Zairean women of Rwandan origin who were expelled to Rwanda said on Friday Zairean troops took 41 of their husbands and sons off trucks and massacred them by the side of the road.
"The Zairean army attacked us and made us board two lorries. said Abiya Nyiradahiriwe, 50, one of the Zairean women who said they were forced from homes in Zaire last week.
"Before the border they took all the men and the male children over 14 off the lorries and massacred all 41 of them with guns at the side of the road," she said.
The women said the incident took place between Uvira and the Rwandan border at Kamanyola.

A total of 107 people but no men or teenage boys arrived at a Pentecostal church outside Gitarama, central Rwanda, last week and were given refuge. They said they had been whipped and beaten by Zairean soldiers.
"We have everything we want here. The only thing we lack is our husbands," one woman said.
"Among that group there were no men and no boys above around 10 which is very disturbing," Paul Stromberg of the U.N. refugee agency UNHCR told Reuters.
UNHCR has not given them refugee status because of their self-described status as 'returnees'.
People who speak Rwanda's national language Kinyarwanda but live in Zaire are at risk following recent Zairean attacks on Rwanda over a border dispute, Rwandan President Pasteur Bizimungu said.

Bizimungu said on Thursday after a conference of U.N. agencies and diplomats: "Since the international community marked the (Rwanda and Zaire) territory, they should take responsibility for solving some of the problems caused by this."
